paper.title: Relative Upper Confidence Bound for the K-Armed Dueling Bandit Problem

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed dueling bandit problem with a Condorcet winner (horizonless setting)
unmapped: Existence of a Condorcet winner a_1 with p_{1i} > 1/2 for all i > 1 (no total ordering or stochastic transitivity required)
Per-round regret r_t = (Delta_i + Delta_j)/2 for compared pair (a_i, a_j), with Delta_k = p_{1k} - 1/2
settings.definition_quote: we choose a pair $(a_i,a_j)$ and receive one of the two as the better choice, with the probability of $a_i$ being picked equal to a constant $p_{ij}$ ... we assume that there exists a \emph{Condorcet winner}: an arm, which without loss of generality we label $a_1$, such that $p_{1i} > \frac{1}{2}$ for all $i>1$. ... regret at that time is set to be $r_t := \frac{\Delta_{1i}+\Delta_{1j}}{2}$, with $\Delta_{k} := p_{1k}-\frac{1}{2}$

bound.regime: simultaneously for all t, any pair (i,j) != (1,1)

symbols.Delta_i: preference gap of arm i: 1/2 - p_{i1} = p_{1i} - 1/2
symbols.Delta_j: preference gap of arm j: 1/2 - p_{j1}

source.label: thm:HighProbBound
source.quote: Then, if we apply Algorithm 1 to the $K$-armed dueling bandit problem defined by $\vP$, given any pair $(i,j) \neq (1,1)$, the number of comparisons between arms $a_i$ and $a_j$ performed up to time $t$, denoted by $N_{ij}(t)$, satisfies P(\forall t, N_{ij}(t) \leq \max\{C(\delta),D_{ij}\ln t\}) > 1-\delta.

results.notes: Bound on number of comparisons of pair (i,j); holds with probability > 1-delta for all t simultaneously. T denotes the current time t. For i = j != 1, D_ii = 0.

symbols.sum_pairs: sum over pairs of arms i > j

source.label: thm:HighProbBound
source.quote: Moreover, we have the following high probability bound for the regret accrued by the algorithm: P(\forall t, R_t \leq C(\delta)\Delta^*+\sum_{i>j} D_{ij} \Delta_{ij} \ln t) > 1-\delta, where $\Delta^* := \max_i \Delta_i$ and $\Delta_{ij} := \frac{\Delta_i+\Delta_j}{2}$

results.notes: D_ij = 4 alpha / min(Delta_i^2, Delta_j^2), C(delta) = ((4alpha-1)K^2/((2alpha-1)delta))^{1/(2alpha-1)}. T is current time t; algorithm is horizonless. Gaps are dueling preference gaps.

symbols.sum_pairs: sum over pairs of arms i > j

source.label: thm:ExpBound
source.quote: Given $\alpha > 1$, the expected regret accumulated by RUCB after $t$ iterations is bounded by \mathbb{E}[R_t] \leq \Delta^*\left(\frac{(4\alpha-1)K^2}{2\alpha-1}\right)^{\frac{1}{2\alpha-1}} \frac{2\alpha-1}{2\alpha-2} +\sum_{i>j}2\alpha\frac{\Delta_i+\Delta_j}{\min\{\Delta_i^2,\Delta_j^2\}}\ln t.

results.notes: Regret defined through preference gaps of compared arms (deterministic given choices), so expectation is pseudo-regret. T denotes iteration count t; horizonless.
